Exercise: Kettlebell Hang Clean

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
pull

Difficulty Level:
intermediate

Movement Patterns:

- hinge
- pull

Primary Muscles:

- hamstrings

Secondary Muscles:

- calves
- glutes
- lower back
- shoulders
- traps

Equipment:

- kettlebells

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
ATP-PC system with some contribution from glycolysis

Recovery Time:
48 hours

Goals:
None

Contraindications:

- condition: Lower back pain, reason: May exacerbate existing conditions due to high load on the spine.
- condition: Shoulder instability, reason: Increased risk of injury due to complex movement and overhead positioning.

Exercise Variations:

- name: Kettlebell Power Clean, notes: Focus on explosive power rather than full range of motion.
- name: Kettlebell Hang Clean to Overhead Press, notes: Add an overhead press at the end of the clean movement.

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Barbell Hang Clean, equipment: barbell
- exercise_name: Dumbbell Hang Clean, equipment: dumbbells

Instructions:

- Place kettlebell between your feet. To get in the starting position, push your butt back and look straight ahead.
- Clean kettlebell to your shoulder. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you raise the kettlebell towards your shoulder. The wrist should rotate as you do so.
- Lower kettlebell to a hanging position between your legs while keeping the hamstrings loaded. Keep your head up at all times.
